findings.evidence: AbstractRolle.lean:106-108 `theorem _root_.Polynomial.exists_derivative_root (p : R[X]) {a b : R} (hab : a < b) (ha : p.eval a = 0) (hb : p.eval b = 0)`; :134-135 `_root_.Polynomial.exists_derivative_root_of_eval_eq ... (h : p.eval a = p.eval b)`; Rolle.lean:43-45 `PolynomialRolle.exists_derivative_root (h : PolynomialRolle R) (p : R[X]) ... (heq : p.eval a = p.eval b)`. Naming conventions, "Identifiers and theorem names": hypotheses are separated by `of`.
findings.fix: Make the base name denote one statement: rename the root-pair version to `Polynomial.exists_derivative_root_of_isRoot` (or `_of_eval_eq_zero`, per the convention that disambiguating hypotheses follow `of`), and let `Polynomial.exists_derivative_root` be the equal-values form matching `PolynomialRolle.exists_derivative_root`.
findings.issue: `Polynomial.exists_derivative_root` takes `(ha : p.eval a = 0) (hb : p.eval b = 0)`, while `TauCeti.PolynomialRolle.exists_derivative_root` (Rolle.lean:43) uses the same base name for the equal-values hypothesis `p.eval a = p.eval b`, and `Polynomial.exists_derivative_root_of_eval_eq` (AbstractRolle.lean:134) is that same equal-values statement under a different name. So `p.exists_derivative_root` and `h.exists_derivative_root` mean different theorems, and the bare `Polynomial` name gives no hint of the root hypothesis it actually needs.

findings.evidence: IVT.lean:43 `theorem _root_.Polynomial.natDegree_le_two_of_irreducible {p : R[X]} (hp : Irreducible p) : p.natDegree ≤ 2`; mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Polynomial/Basic.lean:198 `lemma Irreducible.natDegree_le_two {p : ℝ[X]} (hp : Irreducible p)` (root namespace, dot notation, used as `p.irreducible.natDegree_le_two` in code/TauCeti/RingTheory/Polynomial/RealEtale.lean:261). Every other `_root_.Polynomial.*` in this file takes an explicit `(p : R[X])`, so those escapes are justified; this one is not.
findings.fix: Drop the `_root_.Polynomial.` escape and keep it as `TauCeti.RealClosure.natDegree_le_two_of_irreducible` (matching `TauCeti.coe_rootSet_eq_orbit_of_irreducible`, FieldTheory/GaloisGroups/Stabilizer.lean:141), or state it as genuine dot notation on the irreducibility hypothesis; note a bare `Irreducible.natDegree_le_two` would clash/become ambiguous with Mathlib's ℝ-only lemma, so it needs a distinguishing suffix if you take that route.
findings.issue: `_root_.Polynomial.natDegree_le_two_of_irreducible` escapes into Mathlib's `Polynomial` namespace, but `p` is implicit and the only explicit argument is `hp : Irreducible p`, so neither `p.natDegree_le_two_of_irreducible` nor `hp.…` elaborates — the `Polynomial.` prefix is not dot notation, and the name diverges from Mathlib's own name for this conclusion, `Irreducible.natDegree_le_two`.

summary: The prior round's renames all landed (PolynomialRolle, exists_derivative_root, linear_eval_mul_pos_of_no_roots, IsRoot.exists_eq_pow_succ_mul, polynomialRolle_of_isRealClosed), and the IVT/order/Galois names, the sumSq/exists_linearOrder family and the absence of new notation all check out against Mathlib and repo precedent. Two naming defects remain: the base name `exists_derivative_root` denotes two different statements, and `natDegree_le_two_of_irreducible` is planted in Mathlib's `Polynomial` namespace without being dot notation.
